# UNDERWRITING MEMORANDUM — APA Corporation (APA)

**Prepared by:** Senior Underwriting Board | **As of:** 2026-10-05 | **T0:** $43.68 [live quote, 2026-10-02]

---

## SECTION 0 — OVERVIEW

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Ticker / Company | APA — APA Corporation (Oil & Gas E&P; Permian, Egypt, North Sea, Suriname) |
| Price T0 | $43.68 [Actual, vendor quote 20210-10-02] |
| **Verdict** | **UNDERVALUED** — Base IV is double the price; even the Bear case clears it |
| Base IV (p=0.50) | **$87.37** (+100.0% vs T0) |
| Bull IV (p=0.25) | **$115.51** (+164.4%) |
| Bear IV (p=0.25) | **$51.44** (+17.8%) |
| Probability-weighted IV | $85.42 (+95.6% expected return) [desk] |
| Margin of safety (Base) | +100.0%; (Bear, downside floor) +17.8% |
| Quarter-Kelly (desk) | 24.75% (full Kelly 99.0%, capped); payoff skew 99.9x |
| Capped ledger weight | **8.0%** (High-conviction band cap) |

The market is pricing APA as a company whose cash flow must keep shrinking ~20%/yr through years 3–5 (price-implied, desk reverse DCF). The filings say the opposite: the cost base was locked in during 2026 (run-rate savings raised to ~$500M, LOE guidance cut to $1.5B [PRIMARY P1, 2026-08-05]), and the consensus revenue decline of −9.7% is a one-time fade of the Hormuz-driven price spike, not a trend. That is the crux of this underwriting.

---

## SECTION 1 — MACRO (DATA 1.5 / 1.6)

- **Rates & discounting:** rf 5.24% (10y nominal); COE ANCHOR 8.22%; long-run nominal growth anchor 3.75%; terminal-g default 2.36% (10y breakeven inflation). Curve +0.45% and steepening; IG spread 1.49% — credit is loose, which supports E&P financing and buybacks.
- **Regime vector (2026-09-01):** goldilocks 0.302 / reflation 0.236 / tightening 0.176 / stagflation 0.167 / recession 0.118 — headline goldilocks but **contested** (margin 0.066). For an oil producer, the live swing factor is the commodity shock, not the regime label.
- **ACTIVE SHOCK:** `oil_shock`, severity 1, direction **up**, onset 2026-09-28 [DATA 1.6]. The Strait of Hormuz closure remained unresolved as of 2026-09-30 (Trump rejected a 7-day reopening proposal; Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure; Kazakhstan cannot offset the shortage) [news feed, 2026-09-26/28 — context, not verified]. Brent ran from ~$92 (Aug 19) to >$100 (Sep 10) and ~$108 around Sep 14; partial de-escalation late September with WTI Nov contract ~$91.11 on Sep 29 [secondary, partially **Unconfirmed** levels].
- **Inflation:** CPI 3.35% / PCE 3.42% YoY (2026-10-04) — persistent inflation with markets pricing possible further hikes [news feed] supports real-commodity holders and keeps the terminal-g floor at 2.36%.
- **Exposure:** APA is a pure price-taker with ~flat volumes (reported 410k BOE/d, −12% y/y [PRIMARY P1]); every $10/bbl of WTI moves FY attributable NI by roughly ±$1.5–1.8B at current volumes [Assumption from filed volumes]. The shock cuts both ways: it built 2026 cash flow (Base year 1) and its resolution drives the 2027 fade (Base year 2). No contracted backlog exists to floor the Bear case — APA sells spot commodities; the only quasi-contractual item is Egypt's "revised pricing agreement" covering nearly half of Egypt gas production [PRIMARY P1], which is unquantified in the pack.

---

## SECTION 2 — BUSINESS & MOAT (Mandate 1 deconstruction)

**Engine A — Transactional commodity deliveries (100% of revenue).**
- U.S. Permian: 123,455 bopd oil in Q2-26, raised FY guidance to 123,000 bopd **at flat $1.3B capital** [PRIMARY P1] — volume growth from efficiency, not spend.
- Egypt: 61k BOE/d adjusted (gas-focused; ~half of gas now on the revised pricing agreement) with a 15% NCI drag on consolidated NI (π = 84.8% [DATA 5]).
- North Sea: declining (−30% y/y, 17,676 bopd oil Q2-26 [PRIMARY P1]) — a cash-generating run-off, not a growth engine.
- H1-26 realized prices: total oil $87.89/bbl vs $69.72 in H1-25; U.S. gas realized **negative** (−$1.64/Mcf H1-26) [PRIMARY P1] — hedging/derivative drag is a real margin leak in the U.S. gas book.

**Engine B — Captive annuity: effectively none.** No multi-year contracted backlog or installed base appears in the filings; the "annuity" is the **cost curve itself**: ~$500M exit-2026 run-rate savings (raised from $450M) and LOE guidance cut to $1.5B [PRIMARY P1]. That is a structural margin floor, not recurring revenue — I credit it as margin durability, not contracted cash flow.

**Engine C — Strategic optionality (unpriced in my flows).** Suriname Block 53 (APA operates, 45% WI) and Block 58 (Pau Tom; APA reported a 50% WI with TotalEnergies operator per a 2022 secondary source [**Unconfirmed** — not in pack filings]); Eni strategic partnership on Uruguay OFF-6 and pending Savant (Alaska) acquisition [PRIMARY P1, 2026-08-05; terms **Unconfirmed**]. These are free options; my DCF carries no first-oil cash from them.

**Owner earnings after SBC:** SBC is expensed in GAAP NI and counted once — `sbc_treatment: deducted_in_cf` (no double deduction). Filed SBC is small: $107M FY2025, $84M H1-26 [PRIMARY P1 / DATA 5]. Base owner earnings: **$1.6B** = FY2027 consensus attributable NI ($4.58 EPS × 350.35M shares ≈ $1.60B [Estimate, DATA 8 fetched 2026-10-04]), with D&A (~$2.3B filed FY2025) roughly offsetting maintenance capex ($2.07B 2026 upstream guidance [PRIMARY P1]); conservative vs the ~$1.8B a full D&A/capex offset would imply, and it excludes the H1-26 spike.

**Moat score (7 factors, 0–3 each):**

| Factor | Score | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Cost position | 3 | Top-quartile Permian; $500M run-rate savings locked in [PRIMARY P1] |
| Scale / share | 2 | ~410k BOE/d reported; meaningful independent, not dominant |
| Switching costs / captivity | 1 | Spot commodity sales |
| Asset quality / resources | 3 | Permian + Egypt gas repricing + Suriname/Uruguay options |
| Balance sheet strength | 2 | Net debt $3.3B at Q2-26 [PRIMARY P1], down $2.3B since YE-24; still levered |
| Brand / pricing power | 1 | Price taker |
| Durability vs competitors | 2 | Cost curve durable; commodity ceiling binds |

**Total 14/21 → moat rating 3.7/5.0, direction: improving** (cost base and balance sheet both moved the right way in 2026).

**Financial strength:** OCF $2.26B H1-26; FCF $1.2B H1-26 [PRIMARY P1]; ≥60% of FCF returned to shareholders in 2026 [PRIMARY P1]; $752M near-term debt repaid H1-26, annualized interest down >$155M [PRIMARY P1]; new 40M-share buyback authorization (on top of 19.0M remaining at Jun 30) [**Unconfirmed date**, event confirmed by coverage]. Note: my static 350.35M share count does **not** model the buyback shrinking the base — buying back shares at $43–47 against an $87 intrinsic value is per-share accretion left on the table of this DCF, i.e., the Base is conservative on a per-share basis.

---

## SECTION 3 — VALUATION (every desk input and its departure)

| Input | Value | Default | Departure & reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frame | Equity | Equity | All pack flows are after-interest [charter] |
| base_cf | **$1.6B** | $1.274B | DEFAULTS TTM owner earnings straddle the shock: H2-25 trough (attributable NI ~$0.48B [Arithmetic: FY25 $1.434B − H1-25 $0.950B]) + H1-26 spike ($1.193B, realized oil $87.89/bbl [PRIMARY P1]). Mid-cycle anchor = FY2027 consensus NI ≈ $1.6B [DATA 8, 2026-10-04] with D&A/capex roughly neutral |
| Base growth y1–y5 | **+25%, −20%, +2%, +2%, +2%** | desk would hold y3–5 at −9.7% | y1 = FY2026 spike year (H1-26 NI already $1.193B [PRIMARY P1]); y2 = FY2027 normalization to consensus ($4.58 EPS, −26.9%); **guidance_deviation_reason:** the −9.7% next-FY revenue decline is the one-time fade of the Hormuz spike (realized oil $87.89 vs $69.72 H1-25 [PRIMARY P1]), already carried in y1/y2 — applying it again to years 3–5 would imply a decade of structural decline contradicted by raised U.S. oil guidance at flat capital and cut LOE [PRIMARY P1] |
| Bull growth | +40%, −10%, +5%, +4%, +3% | — | Closure persists through 2026 (WTI ~$100; consensus FY26 EPS $6.27 ≈ $2.2B NI), then OPEC+ discipline holds WTI ~$80 into 2027 (next-FY estimate trend +7.7% in 90 days [DATA 8]) |
| Bear growth | +20%, −35%, −3%, −2%, −1% | — | Closure resolves Q3-26 (y1 still elevated), then glut to WTI ~$60–65 (FY2025 levels); $500M cost base cushions the fall; +128bp rate shock (9.50%) |
| fade_years | 3 (Bull 4, Bear 5) | — | Fade from explicit to terminal over the reserve-replacement runway |
| terminal_g | 2.36% | 2.36% | No departure |
| terminal_ronic | 13.53% | 13.53% | No departure (record median r_tc 16.71%, p=0.625, 2019–2025 [DEFAULTS]) |
| CoE | 8.22% Base/Bull; 9.50% Bear | 8.22% | Anchor for Base (no coe_adjustment_reason needed); Bear carries the +100–200bp credit-tightening stress of mandate 4 |
| Shares | 350,351,510 | same | No contingent instruments vest in any scenario |
| Excess cash | $437M (default) | same | Added per share by the desk |
| Cash-flow life | **Perpetual** | — | FY2025 additions to PP&E $2.673B > D&A $2.304B [PRIMARY P3, filed 2026-02-26] — the reserve stock is replaced by capex my flows already deduct (2026 upstream capital $2.07B [PRIMARY P1]). **Price deck:** H1-26 realized oil $87.89/bbl vs H1-25 $69.72 [PRIMARY P1]; Base assumes normalization to ~$70–75 WTI by FY2027 (WTI Nov ~$91 on 2026-09-29 [Unconfirmed level]) |
| Probabilities | 0.50 / 0.25 / 0.25 | — | Hormuz resolution timing is the swing factor: partial de-escalation already observed (WTI Nov ~$91, Sep 29) but renewed closure risk reported Sep 30 [news feed] — symmetric odds on prolonged spike vs early unwind; Base = the consensus normalization path |

**Desk terminal:** Gordon on funded earnings at CoE 8.22%, g 2.36%, terminal ROIC fading from 16.71% to 13.53% → **implied terminal EV/FCF 17.47x (Base/Bull), 14.34x (Bear)**. Terminal value is 64% of Base value — the single largest sensitivity. Cross-check: cluster peer trailing P/E median 10.8x, p75 18.6x [DATA 8.5]; APA at T0 trades at **9.5x FY2027E EPS** (below the cluster median) and ~11.6x EV/forward FCF — so the market is not paying a rich multiple today; it is paying for *decline*. The 17.5x terminal multiple sits ~50–60% above the peer median P/E; I accept the desk's funded-earnings multiple because APA's own record supports it (r_tc 16.7% median, top-quartile cost curve), but the gap is stated plainly: if the market insists on a 12x terminal multiple, Base value falls materially — this is carried in the Bear case, which still clears T0 at $51.44 with a 14.3x implied terminal.

**Reverse DCF (mandatory, mandate 3b):**
- Own structure: price implies **Stage-1 growth of −12.0%/yr** over the next 5 years.
- Neutral reference (anchor CoE 8.22%, terminal-g 3.75%, 10-year fade): solved initial growth **−18.73%**, **10-year CAGR −6.59%**.
- Base-rate band: **not available** — the corpus holds no size bucket or consecutive revenue pair for APA (revenue NA in the filed XBRL series [DATA 5]). In its place, company-specific dated evidence: raised U.S. oil guidance to 123,000 bopd at flat $1.3B capital; LOE cut to $1.5B; exit run-rate savings raised to ~$500M [PRIMARY P1, 2026-08-05]. No E&P with a locked-in cost base and reserve replacement (capex > D&A [PRIMARY P3]) needs to be priced for perpetual shrinkage.

**Price-implied judgments (desk):** coe **14.97%** vs my 8.22% (the price only reconciles if APA's risk is ~675bp higher than the anchor implies); growth_years_3_5 **−20.2%/yr** vs my +2.0%/yr; fade_years, terminal_g (bound to 4.47%) and terminal_ronic: **not reachable** — no value of the terminal inputs inside their bounds brings Base down to T0. The price is below Base on *any* admissible terminal assumption; the only live disagreements are growth and discount rate.

**Crux (verdict support, TASK item 6):**
- **Input:** `growth_years_3_5` — **mine: +2.0%/yr; price implies −20.2%/yr** (a ~22pp/yr gap across years 3–5).
- **Why the price is wrong:** it treats the next-FY consensus revenue decline of −9.7% as a permanent trend.
